rendered.overview: This Non-black, five-identity Aang deck leans on bending: Lessons, earthbend and airbend effects feed [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], which draws on each bend and transforms once all four are done. It wins through flying attacks, counters on Allies, and the transform's 4 damage. [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] is an alternate loop.

Earthbends on every spell cast.
Airbends permanents and makes Ally tokens.
Airbends on entering; part of the loop.
Fixes colors for lands and Allies.
Finds Lessons and grows creatures.
Puts counters on every creature.

weaknesses: Moderate: Several enchantments and artifacts power the deck, and [[Vandalblast]] would hit them.
Moderate: Only 2 interaction cards, 1 at instant speed, so a fast combo from [[Thassa's Oracle]] gets through.
Moderate: Without [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] the card flow and the transform damage stop.

avatar aang // aang, master of elements.name: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements

plans.primary: Build a board of Allies and earthbent lands while [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] draws cards off every bend, then transform it to hit each opponent for 4 and attack in the air.
backups: Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for infinite creature enters, leaves and tokens with 1 mana.

reply.overview: This Non-black, five-identity Aang deck leans on bending: Lessons, earthbend and airbend effects feed [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], which draws on each bend and transforms once all four are done. It wins through flying attacks, counters on Allies, and the transform's 4 damage. [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] is an alternate loop.

strategy.text: Ramp with [[Bender's Waterskin]], [[Chromatic Lantern]] and [[Great Divide Guide]] to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Trigger bends with [[Earthbending Lesson]], [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] and airbend spells so the commander draws cards.
Fill the board with Allies and counters using [[Southern Air Temple]] and [[Guru Pathik]] while holding up Lesson interaction.
Transform the commander after all four bends, then swing in the air for the 4 damage and drawn cards.
Alternate win: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] make infinite enters, leaves and tokens.

keep.text: [[Great Divide Guide]] with a second mana source ramps toward the commander.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] plus a cheap Lesson starts the bend triggers.

sendBack.text: Hands with only expensive Lessons and no early mana or creatures.
Hands missing white or blue sources for the five-color spells.

tips.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] airbends your permanents, then each recast from exile makes a 1/1 Ally token.
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles [[Haru, Hidden Talent]]'s trigger, so each Ally entering earthbends twice.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbends on every spell you cast, and each earthbend draws a card from [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]].

assessment.line: Lesson payoffs like [[Gran-Gran]] and [[Bumi, King of Three Trials]] count the graveyard, so [[Bojuka Bog]] slows them.
Several enchantments and artifacts power the deck, and [[Vandalblast]] would hit them.

Wins lean on creature attacks, so [[Propaganda]] slows the plan.
The backup loop needs [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and removal on it breaks it.
Lands make no black, and many basics against five colors need [[Chromatic Lantern]] to fix.

rendered.overview: Jeskai artifacts built around [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], a haste artifact creature that proliferates whenever it taps. Counters pile up on artifacts and creatures until [[Lux Artillery]] deals 10 damage or [[Dragonspark Reactor]] fires, with extra-turn and infinite-draw combos as alternate routes.

strategy: Ramp with rocks and artifact lands, then cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3.
Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] each turn to proliferate, with [[Surge Conductor]] adding more on each artifact.
Grow counters with [[Steel Overseer]] and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]], which doubles proliferate.
Finish with 10 damage from [[Lux Artillery]] or by sacrificing [[Dragonspark Reactor]].
Alternate win: [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] make infinite turns.

keep: [[Surge Conductor]] with cheap artifacts to trigger it.
Mana rocks that pave the way to [[Steel Overseer]].
sendBack: Expensive proliferate pieces and no cheap artifact to start.
Hands missing blue or white for the artifact spells.

tips.text: [[Steel Overseer]] taps to add counters on artifact creatures, and [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] makes artifact creatures bigger still.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles each proliferate from [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] tapping.
[[Lux Artillery]] wants thirty counters, and [[Contagion Engine]] proliferates twice for four mana.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever it taps.
Proliferates when artifacts enter.
Doubles every proliferate.
Grows artifact creatures each turn.
Deals 10 damage at thirty counters.
Turns artifact counters into damage.
Extra turns from charge counters.
Proliferates twice for four mana.

weaknesses: Critical: A sweep like [[Vandalblast]] hits most of the artifacts and the engine, and the deck has little enchantment answer.
Moderate: Removal such as [[Swords to Plowshares]] on [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] stops the proliferate engine.
Moderate: Wins rely on counters, so [[Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider]] halving them slows the plan.

plans.primary: Build an artifact and counter pile around [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], proliferating every time it taps until [[Lux Artillery]] or [[Dragonspark Reactor]] finishes the table.
backups: Assemble [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns and a lock.
Pair [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] for infinite draw triggers and looting.

rendered.overview: This Colorless artifact and Eldrazi deck ramps with rocks and utility lands, then casts [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5 to cascade twice off its expensive colorless spells. It wins with annihilator Eldrazi and big artifact creatures. [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana.

strategy: Play [[Sol Ring]], [[Thran Dynamo]] and other rocks early to reach six mana fast.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] so colorless spells from hand with mana value 7 or greater cascade twice.
Land [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]] and attack so annihilator strips the table.
Alternate win: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Thran Dynamo]] or [[Palladium Myr]] with a land to cast it.
sendBack: Expensive Eldrazi with no ramp to cast them.

tips.text: [[Eye of Ugin]] cuts colorless Eldrazi costs, so [[Artisan of Kozilek]] is cheaper and it can fetch big colorless creatures.
[[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] taps for extra {C} each, so you can untap it repeatedly.
[[It That Betrays]] puts nontoken permanents opponents sacrifice to [[Artisan of Kozilek]]'s annihilator onto your side.

keyCards.job: Gives big colorless spells double cascade.
Cheapens Eldrazi and finds colorless creatures.
Reanimates on cast and attacks with annihilator.
Steals what annihilator makes opponents sacrifice.
Mana source and half of the infinite mana pair.
Doubles colorless mana for infinite mana.
Clears colored permanents of the table.

weaknesses: Moderate: Many rocks and artifact creatures fall to [[Vandalblast]] or [[Null Rod]], and the deck has few ways to answer enchantments.
Moderate: Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed, so a fast combo gets past except what [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] can counter.
Minor: Colorless-only lands mean [[Ugin, the Ineffable]] and other colored permanents of opponents hit hard, and nonbasic land hate like [[Blood Moon]] hurts.

backups: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana.
[[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] exiles every colored permanent while the deck's colorless permanents stay.

rendered.overview: This Naya Dinosaur deck ramps into big trampling creatures and cheats more of them onto the battlefield with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and [[Pantlaza, Sun-Favored]]. It wins by attacking with a wide Dinosaur board, with infinite-token lines through [[Polyraptor]] as an alternate route.

strategy: Ramp with [[Atzocan Seer]], [[Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea]] and [[Topiary Stomper]] toward big Dinosaurs and the commander.
Cast cheap Dinosaurs, helped by [[Kinjalli's Caller]] and [[Knight of the Stampede]], to fill the board.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to reveal cards and drop Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Swing with trampling Dinosaurs, pumped by [[Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma]] and [[Quartzwood Crasher]].
Backup: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] together make infinite tokens and damage.

keep: [[Atzocan Seer]] or [[Great Forest Druid]] with a Dinosaur to cast.
sendBack: Expensive Dinosaurs with no ramp or colored sources.

tips.text: [[Polyraptor]] copies itself when damaged, so [[Forerunner of the Empire]] pinging each creature makes endless tokens.
[[Bellowing Aegisaur]] triggers when [[Walking Ballista]] pings it, adding counters to your other creatures.
[[Boxing Ring]] makes each entering creature fight, setting off [[Ripjaw Raptor]] enrage draws.

keyCards.job: Commander that puts Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Discovers more spells when Dinosaurs enter.
Finds Dinosaurs and starts the Polyraptor loop.
Copies itself whenever it is damaged.
Cuts big creature costs and boosts attackers.
Makes Beasts and casts creatures from the top.
Pings Dinosaurs to trigger enrage effects.

weaknesses: Moderate: Seven interaction cards with none at instant speed cannot stop a fast combo such as [[Thassa's Oracle]] in time.
Moderate: Wins mostly through combat, so a fog or [[Propaganda]] stalls the whole Dinosaur army.
Minor: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] costs eight, so repeated removal or taxing leaves the deck relying on its other Dinosaurs.

plans.primary: Cast [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and connect in combat to put Dinosaurs from the top of the library onto the battlefield, then win with a wide trampling Dinosaur army.
backups: Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] to make infinite Polyraptor tokens and ping every creature.
Pair [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] with [[Walking Ballista]] for infinite +1/+1 counters on your creatures.

rendered.overview: This mono-red Goblin deck is built around [[Krenko, Mob Boss]], which doubles the Goblin count every turn. Cheap Goblins and token makers feed it, haste enablers like [[Goblin Chieftain]] turn the horde into attackers, and burn such as [[Fireball]] and [[Goblin Bombardment]] finishes the game.

strategy: Play cheap Goblins like [[Mogg War Marshal]] and [[Dragon Fodder]] to build a board before the commander arrives.
Cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 and tap it each turn to double the Goblins.
Give the horde haste with [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] and swing, or sacrifice Goblins to [[Goblin Bombardment]].
Alternate win: [[Goblin Warchief]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] make infinite commander casts and hasty tokens.

keep: [[Mogg War Marshal]] or [[Dragon Fodder]] with early ramp builds toward the commander.
[[Goblin Matron]] fetching a lord gets the Goblin plan started.
sendBack: Hands of only burn spells lack the Goblins that [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] multiplies.
Expensive spells without early ramp or cheap Goblins stall the plan.

tips.text: [[Goblin Chieftain]] gives the new tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] haste, so they can attack the turn they appear.
[[Pashalik Mons]] pings for each Goblin sacrificed to [[Goblin Bombardment]], so every sacrifice deals 2 damage.
[[Goblin Matron]] can fetch [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] to set up the haste payoff.

keyCards.job: Doubles the Goblin count every turn.
Fetches a lord or key Goblin.
Makes two bodies for the commander.
Gives Goblins haste and +1/+1.
Discounts Goblins and grants haste.
Sacrifices Goblins for mana in the loop.
Turns tokens into damage.
Pings whenever a Goblin dies.

weaknesses: Moderate: Without [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] the token count stops growing, and repeated removal like [[Swords to Plowshares]] slows the deck.
Moderate: Wins lean on small attackers, so a sweeper like [[Anger of the Gods]] or a fog undoes the board.
Minor: [[Goblin Bombardment]] and [[Sulfuric Vortex]] have no answer here if an opponent destroys them with something like [[Disenchant]].

plans.primary: Cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and tap it each turn to double the Goblin count, then swing with a hasty horde or burn opponents out with the tokens.
backups: Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite commander casts, hasty tokens and death triggers.

rendered.overview: A Jeskai partner deck led by [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]. Gods and attacks feed experience counters, which become +1/+1 counters, and proliferate pieces such as [[Inexorable Tide]] grow them further. [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] drains for 2 and draws, while extra combats and burn finish the game.

strategy: Cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] around turn 4, backed by rocks and Gods to attack with.
Attack with Gods or let them die to gain experience, so [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] adds counters at your end step.
Proliferate with [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Flux Channeler]] to grow experience and +1/+1 counters.
Use [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] and [[All Will Be One]] to drain opponents as counters accumulate.
Backup: [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] give extra combats to finish with a large team.

keep: [[Talisman of Progress]] plus a God ready to attack.
[[Inexorable Tide]] with early plays to proliferate.
sendBack: Hands with no way to cast a God or reach both our colors.
Several expensive spells and no early ramp.

tips.text: [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds an extra counter whenever [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] gives you experience.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] makes each proliferate from [[Inexorable Tide]] happen twice.

keyCards.job: Turns experience into +1/+1 counters each end step.
Drains for 2 and loots per experience counter.
Proliferates on every spell cast.
Adds extra counters to our creatures and us.
Gains experience and makes attacking Rebels.
Turns each counter placed into damage.
Gives extra combat phases for the team.

weaknesses: Moderate: Many enchantments and Gods fall to [[Farewell]], and the deck has no clear answer to opposing artifacts.
Moderate: Counter growth relies on [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], and removal like [[Path to Exile]] on it slows the plan.
Moderate: Combat-heavy wins stall against [[Propaganda]] or fogs.

backups: Chain [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] for extra combats with a counter-boosted team.
Deal direct damage with [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]], [[All Will Be One]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] as counters pile up.

rendered.overview: [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] leads a mono-blue Wizard deck full of counterspells, cantrips and cheap flash creatures. It stalls opposing plays, loots off every counter, and wins through [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] combos, [[Triskaidekaphile]], or a self-mill finish with [[Laboratory Maniac]].

strategy: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 so every instant and sorcery costs one less.
Hold up [[Counterspell]], [[Mana Leak]] and [[Memory Lapse]], looting off each counter through [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]].
Refill with [[Archmage of Runes]], [[Brainstorm]] and [[Thirst for Knowledge]] while the table spends its resources.
Close with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] copying [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite triggers, or [[Ghostly Flicker]] with it at seven mana.
Alternate win: [[Brain Freeze]] empties the library, then [[Laboratory Maniac]] wins on the next draw.

keep: [[Archmage of Runes]] with a counterspell and cheap blue mana.
[[Preordain]] plus a cheap counter smooths the early turns.
sendBack: Expensive creatures and no counterspell or cantrip to interact early.
A lone [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with nothing to copy.

tips.text: Cast [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with flash while [[Sublime Epiphany]] is on the stack to copy it for extra modes.
[[Ghostly Flicker]] can target [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] and another creature to copy a spell again on each return.
[[Brain Freeze]] gains storm copies from cheap spells made cheaper by [[Jace's Sanctum]].

keyCards.job: Cheapens spells and loots on counters.
Draws a card on each instant or sorcery.
Copies a spell and powers combos.
Flexible counter that pairs with Naru Meha.
Blinks Naru Meha for repeated triggers.
Cheap hard counter that triggers Baral.

rendered.overview: Dimir ninjas deck led by [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]]. Cheap unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Triton Shorestalker]] connect, then ninjutsu creatures such as [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] swap in for card advantage and life loss. Counterspells and cheap removal protect the attack, and extra turns add more combats.

strategy: Cast cheap unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Changeling Outcast]] to attack early.
Return the unblocked attacker with ninjutsu to put in [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] or [[Ingenious Infiltrator]] for cards.
Put [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] in from the command zone so each ninja hit reveals cards and drains opponents.
Hold counterspells such as [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] to protect the attackers.
Backup: chain extra turns with [[Temporal Manipulation]] and [[Time Warp]] for more combat steps.

keep: [[Mistblade Shinobi]] with an unblockable creature and blue mana.
Cheap ninjutsu plus [[Slither Blade]] starts the attacks early.
sendBack: Hands with only expensive ninjas and no unblockable attacker.
Hands missing blue or black sources for ninjutsu.

tips.text: [[Higure, the Still Wind]] searches for a Ninja on a hit, finding [[Throat Slitter]] to remove blockers.
[[Silver-Fur Master]] cuts ninjutsu costs by 1, making [[Fallen Shinobi]] cheaper to put in.
[[Thousand-Faced Shadow]] copies an attacker, so pair it with [[Mist-Syndicate Naga]] to multiply ninjas.
